summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of endometriosis was admitted for severe left lower quadrant pain radiating to the rectum and left leg, consistent with an acute exacerbation of chronic endometriosis pain. Initial presentation included tachycardia with a heart rate of 158, attributed to pain. A CT scan was performed due to elevated lactate, revealing a small hemorrhagic ovarian cyst but no evidence of infection, ischemia, or other acute intra-abdominal pathology. Pain was managed with intravenous dilaudid, morphine, and toradol, followed by transition to oral medications. The gabapentin dose was increased, tizanidine was added, and the patient received a Lupron injection prior to discharge. She improved significantly, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up instructions and new prescriptions. No procedures were performed during the admission.
